title: CRLR/14/2015 of Jakir Hussain AND ANOTHER Vs State Of Uttarakhand

paras.text:
CRLR No. 14 of 2015
With
CRLR No. 232 of 2014
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Mohd. Matloob, Advocate for the
revisionists.
Mr. Siddhartha Bisth, Brief Holder for
the State of Uttarakhand.
Mr. Mehboob Ravi, Advocate for the
complainant.
These are two connected Criminal
Revisions arising out of the judgment dated
5
th August, 2014, as passed by the learned
Sessions Judge, Udham Singh Nagar in
Criminal Case No. 56 of 2014, Jakir Hussain
and another Vs. State of Uttarakhand as well
as the judgment dated 24th January, 2014, as
passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate,
Kashipur in Criminal Case No. 260 of 2013,
State Vs. Jakir Hussain and another, which
was arising out of Case Crime No. 15 of 2013,
by virtue of which, for the offence under
Section 25 (kha) (ka), of the Arms Act, the
appellants have been convicted and awarded a
sentence of three years R.I. and a fine of
Rs.1,000/- each has been imposed and in
default of payment of fine, the appellants have
been directed to further undergo one month
simple imprisonment.
The second Revision which is
connected, being Criminal Revision No. 232
of 2014, Jakir Hussain and another Vs. State
of Uttarakhand. The said Criminal Revision
arises out of the judgment dated 5th August,
2014, passed by the Sessions Judge, Udham
Singh Nagar, whereby, the Sessions Judge
rejected the Criminal Appeal and has affirmed
the judgment and order dated 24.01.2014,
passed by the Judicial Magistrate, Kashipur in
Criminal Case No. 198 of 2013. For the

offence under Section 394 I.P.C., the
appellants have been convicted to undergo a
sentence of three years R.I. and a fine of
Rs.1,000/- and in default of payment of fine,
the appellants have been directed to undergo
further one month simple imprisonment; for
the offence under Section 411 I.P.C., the
appellants have been convicted to undergo a
sentence of two years R.I. and a fine of
Rs.1,000/- each and in default of payment of
fine, the appellants have to undergo further
one month simple imprisonment; and for the
offence under Section 452 I.P.C., the
appellants have been convicted to undergo a
sentence of two years R.I. and a fine of
Rs.1,000/- each and in default of payment of
fine, the appellants have to undergo further
one month simple imprisonment.
In pursuance to the impugned order
under challenge, the revisionists have
preferred the present Revisions before this
Court.
When the matter came up for
consideration at the admission stage, the
Court while admitting the Revision and
considering the fact that out of total sentence
of three years, which has been imposed upon
the revisionists, since the revisionists have
already undergone and served the sentence of
25 months as against the maximum
punishment of three years, the revisionists
were granted bail.
In view of the fact that the major part of
the sentence as imposed by both the Courts
below have already been undergone by the
revisionists by serving the sentence of 25
months, the Revisions would stand allowed on
that ground itself, that the major part of the
sentence has already been undergone by the
revisionists. However, the penalty as
imposed upon the revisionists by the Court

below that is directed to be deposited by the
revisionists with the Magistrate concerned, if
not already deposited.
The revisionists are on bail, as a
consequence of the order passed by the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court on 1st June,
2019. The revisionists need not to surrender
and the sureties as furnished for the purpose
of granting the bail in compliance of the order
dated 1st June, 2015 and that the same would
stand discharged.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
Dated 23.07.2019
Shiv
